item.title: Fermionic Condensation as the Universal Order Parameter for Mass Generation
item.description: arXiv:2610.28654v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A fermion bilinear acquiring a non-zero vacuum expectation value and generating a mass gap underlies the Peierls instability, BCS superconductivity, the Nambu--Jona-Lasinio mechanism, and the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model. These mechanisms are usually discussed separately, and their structural similarities have been noted only in passing. We argue here that the correct universal object is not the bosonic order parameter but the fermionic condensate, and we show that the four mechanisms fall into two universality classes distinguished by a single dimensionless parameter, $r = \hat m_\phi^2 / \hat y^2$, the ratio of the scalar mass to the Yukawa coupling. The classes are separated by a critical line $r_c(N_f)$ in the plane of $r$ and the fermion flavour number $N_f$; they correspond to two distinct infrared fixed points of the renormalisation-group flow and differ in their critical exponents. We derive the classification from a large-$N_f$ expansion followed by a functional renormalisation-group analysis using the Wetterich equation, which gives the finite-$N_f$ correction $\hat y_*^2(N_f) = 0.1125/N_f + 0.0023/N_f^2$, a $12.5\%$ enhancement over the leading-order prediction. The classification is predictive for systems whose class is not already known; for the organic conductor (TMTSF)$_2$PF$_6$ under pressure, we predict that both the spin-density-wave and superconducting phases lie in the fermion-bilinear class. We discuss the Standard Model Higgs as a borderline case in the scalar-primary class, and identify the composite-Higgs scenario as the particle-physics realisation of the fermion-bilinear class. A self-consistent Su--Schrieffer--Heeger calculation for polyyne chains realises the Peierls mechanism concretely, and we list five falsifiable predictions, two within reach of current techniques.
item.dc:creator: Aniekan Magnus Ukpong

item.title: Viscous matter in modified $f(R)$-gravity: Hubble tension attenuation with DESI and SH0ES data
item.description: arXiv:2610.28659v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the late-time dynamics of the Universe in a modified metric $f(R)$ gravity model formulated in the Jordan frame. The standard $\Lambda$CDM model is additionally deformed to include a non-equilibrium effect on matter dynamics, represented via a bulk viscosity coefficient. We impose an additional condition on the cosmological dynamics that allows the matter energy density, the non-minimally coupled scalar field, and its non-constant potential to be treated as dynamical variables. In this way, the form of the $f(R)$ model is not specified \emph{a priori}, but is instead dynamically reconstructed from the evolution of the system. The resulting model contains five free parameters and is tested against Type Ia supernova and DESI data, using the SH0ES calibration for the supernova sample and a Planck calibration for the sound horizon. We find that the data mainly constrain the standard cosmological parameters $H_0$ and $\Omega_{m0}$, while the three additional parameters remain only weakly constrained and are further restricted by imposing the physical viability conditions of the model. Our main result is that the model can accommodate SN Ia and DESI observations while allowing a larger value of $H_0$ than in the corresponding $\Lambda$CDM analysis and keeping the acoustic horizon close to the Planck value.
item.dc:creator: Elisa Fazzari, Nakia Carlevaro, Giovanni Montani

item.title: Recovering What Breaks in a Trapped-Ion Quantum Simulation of a Lattice Gauge Theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.28660v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A recent trapped-ion experiment realised a lattice gauge theory with the gauge field in the internal states of the ions and bosonic matter in their vibrations. We showed earlier that its noise damage can be predicted. Here, we show that most of it can be undone. The conservation law of the theory is a parity of each vibrational mode, which heating flips, so a heating event leaves a mark that can be read without disturbing the physics. We keep only the runs in which this mark never changed. With equal heating rates and continuous monitoring, the kept runs reproduce the heating-free dynamics exactly, with a closed-form yield. Reading the mark at finite intervals introduces a small bias linear in the interval, which we derive and bound. At the reported rates, a single final check removes most of the heating and preparation damage while accepting eight runs out of ten.
item.dc:creator: Hassan Ugail

item.title: Swampland diagnostics and observational tests of the inflationary universe in the Palatini formalism
item.description: arXiv:2610.28661v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider quintessential inflation in a quadratic Palatini model with a generalized Peebles-Vilenkin potential, where the same scalar field describes both the inflationary plateau and the later inverse-power-law regime. Passing to the Einstein frame gives a canonically normalized field and an explicit effective potential. The inflationary predictions are then reassessed, together with the further-refined de Sitter, scalar weak-gravity, strong scalar weak-gravity, distance, and trans-Planckian censorship conjectures. The value of the tensor-to-scalar ratio stays below the observational bounds used in this work, whereas the spectral index of scalar fluctuations changes with the potential exponent and with the duration of inflation. The further-refined de Sitter bound is satisfied only over part of the trajectory. At the pivot, both weak-gravity diagnostics are negative in the reduced-Planck-mass convention, although they become positive at finite field values. The field excursion is super-Planckian, but this does not by itself imply a failure of the distance conjecture; the trans-Planckian censorship criterion is not met in the assumed slow-roll regime.
item.dc:creator: Saeed Noori Gashti, Mohammad Reza Alipour, Mohammad Ali S. Afshar, Kazuharu Bamba

item.title: A general criterion to compare metric and Palatini formulations with arbitrary non-minimal couplings: the case of Natural Inflation
item.description: arXiv:2610.28662v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Natural Inflation with several types of non-minimal couplings to gravity in metric and Palatini formalisms, focusing on how the choice of gravitational formulation affects inflationary observables. Starting from a Jordan-frame action with a general coupling function $\gamma^2(\phi)$, we examine several representative cases: periodic couplings ($\sin$ and $\cos$) and power-law couplings ($\phi^n$ with $n = 1, 2, -2$). To track differences between the two formalisms, we employ a diagnosis parameter $J$ defined as ${J}\equiv K_{\rm M}/K_{\rm P} -1$, where $K_{\rm M}$ and $K_{\rm P}$ are the kinetic functions in the Einstein frame in both formalisms. This parameter directly quantifies the relative enhancement of the kinetic sector in the metric formulation. For the aforementioned couplings, we compute predictions for the spectral index $n_s$ and tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$, compare them against Planck 2018 and ACT DR6 observational constraints in both formalisms. Extending the particular cases mentioned before, we derive a general classification of arbitrary coupling functions for small-field inflation depending on the behavior of $J$ at reference values during inflation: Case I with vanishing ${J}$, so, both formalisms become nearly degenerate; and Case II with non-vanishing ${J}$ for which residual differences persist when evaluated at field values consistent with inflationary expansion. We find that periodic couplings are disfavored by data, whereas power-law couplings can achieve agreement for specific parameter ranges. Notably, in all the cases we found that Natural Inflation consistent with slow-roll evolution has $J$ either vanishing or strongly suppressed; consequently, switching the gravitational formulation yields no improvement for its observational viability.
item.dc:creator: Andres Felipe Suarez Reyes, Juan P. Beltr\'an Almeida

item.title: Cosmological Bounds on the Generalized Uncertainty Principle from the CMB
item.description: arXiv:2610.28664v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We constrain the deformation parameter $\beta$ of the Generalized Uncertainty Principle with cosmological observations. A quadratic deformation of the Heisenberg uncertainty principle modifies the Friedmann equations of $\Lambda $CDM and gives rise to a phenomenological dynamical dark energy with a single free parameter, $\beta$. To avoid a singular behaviour for the effective dark energy equation of state parameter, we restrict the prior to non-negative values of $\beta$. Using Planck 2018 CMB temperature and polarization data together with DESI DR2 BAO and Pantheon+SH0ES supernovae, we find the upper limit $\beta<0.00728~$ at $68\%$ confidence interval. The resulting cosmological model fits the data slightly better than $\Lambda$CDM, providing smaller value for the $\chi_{min}^{2}% $, such that the Akaike Information Criterion to suggest statistical equivalency between the two models, although the Bayesian evidence favours the $\Lambda$CDM. Finally, the quadratic Generalized Uncertainty Principle does not alleviate the $H_{0}$ tension, it reduces the tension to $4.8\sigma$, that is, due to the small correlation between the $H_{0}-\beta$ parameters.
item.dc:creator: Andronikos Paliathanasis

item.title: Towards a Complete Kerr Soft-Hair Theory: Integrability, Counterterm Equivalence,and Quantum State Counting
item.description: arXiv:2610.28700v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The horizon symmetry construction of Haco, Hawking, Perry, and Strominger yield two Virasoro central charges 12J after a specified Wald-Zoupas correction. Turning that calculation into a black hole microstate theory requires separate control of nonlinear charge integrability, the allowed counter-term class, and quantum state multiplicities. We formulate exact local and global integrability tests, prove uniqueness of the counter-term coefficients within a one-parameter ansatz, and identify the quotient in which a physically meaningful uniqueness theorem must be stated. A coadjoint-orbit model supplies globally defined classical moment maps, while unitary highest-weight modules supply an explicit algebraic quantum realization for macroscopic positive angular momentum, neither construction is proved equivalent to the gravitational phase space. A character calculation shows why a single Virasoro representation, despite having the desired central charge, does not provide the required large-central-charge entropy. We derive a curvature improvement invisible to the constant mode, quantize a regulated area-boost corner polarization, and find a continuous kinematic spectrum with divergent Gibbs trace. Explicit local modular CFT spectra with identical central charges yield different finite-temperature entropies, demonstrating that the available symmetry and quantum consistency data do not select the microscopic theory. We give a conditional sufficiency theorem and a concrete sequence of calculations needed to establish a gravitational completion.
item.dc:creator: Sandi Setiawan

item.title: Tetrads and their intrinsic spin structures
item.description: arXiv:2610.28713v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In Minkowski spacetime an observer's moving frame may be associated with a tetrad: four orthogonal directions, one timelike and three spacelike. Locally, a physical measurement is always made in relation to some tetrad, and relativistic spin measurements in particular raise subtleties because spin and momentum cannot be cleanly separated under Lorentz boosts. This paper shows that every tetrad is endowed with an intrinsic spin structure. Each spatial direction may be generated from the timelike direction by a linear operator, and the requirement that these generate an orthogonal tetrad for every timelike direction is sufficient, on its own, to endow them with the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{so}(1,3)$, the Pauli algebra $\mathrm{Cl}_{3,0}(\mathbb{R})$ and the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ simultaneously. These generators serve three roles at once: they build the spatial legs of every tetrad, they generate the Lorentz boosts between tetrads, and they endow each tetrad with an intrinsic spin structure. The eigenvectors of the spin generators form a null-ray tetrad which is simultaneously a Newman--Penrose-type frame and the set of Dirac rest spinors, while the invertibility of boosts between tetrads yields the Dirac factorisation of the mass-shell condition. Minimal coupling of gauge and spinor fields is forced rather than imposed, the potential being absorbed by the covariant derivative because the path dependence of the phase prevents it from being incorporated by the spinor phase. Wigner rotations, relativistic spin correlations, quantum reference frames and the Coulomb problem are examined within this tetrad framework. This framework is equivalent to the Hilbert-space formalism of relativistic quantum mechanics wherever the two have been compared, and so offers a geometric formulation of that formalism rather than an alternative to it.
item.dc:creator: Tony Lyons

item.title: Sweep-Direction-Dependent Level-Attraction- and Level-Repulsion-Like Signatures in a Twisted, Helically Corrugated Microwave Resonator
item.description: arXiv:2610.29321v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate photon--photon interactions in a mechanically tunable, helically corrugated rectangular microwave resonator. Mechanical twisting modifies the electromagnetic helicity and resonant frequencies of the supported modes, allowing pairs of electromagnetic modes to be tuned into near-degeneracy. Transmission magnitude and phase measurements reveal two distinct responses: a level-attraction-like response characterised by converging antiresonances and a sharp phase variation appearing as a $2\pi$ discontinuity in the wrapped transmission phase, and a level-repulsion-like response characterised by an anticrossing-like transmission feature. For the mode-interaction regions investigated, reversing the twist sweep direction interchanges these responses. We discuss mechanical hysteresis and changes in electromagnetic backscattering and modal interference as possible origins of this behaviour. These observations suggest a potential route towards microwave devices with mechanically switchable level-attraction-like and level-repulsion-like transmission responses.
item.dc:creator: Emma C. I. Paterson, Jeremy Bourhill

item.title: Gravitational Redshift of Light and the Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle
item.description: arXiv:2604.09662v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Empirical observations together with theoretical analyses are being used to argue that the classical phenomenon of gravitational redshift -- namely, the redshift of light in a static gravitational potential -- may be in tension with the Heisenberg uncertainty principle. In particular, in the Pound-Rebka experiment, the emitter-absorber pair interact with each other by exchanging a Mossbauer photon, a process that is fully describable within quantum mechanics but how the photon interacts with the spacetime metric remains unclear. Since the uncertainty principle is incompatible with local realism, as per general relativity, we propose to study continuous-variable photonic entanglement within the Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen (EPR) framework in a weak gravitational field. We outline a thought experiment, realizable on the surface of the Earth, that could shed further light on this problematic seamline between general relativity and quantum mechanics in the weak-field regime.
item.dc:creator: Asher Klatchko, Robert Hill

item.title: A Machine Learning Approach to Finslerian Cosmological Dark Energy Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.26882v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Modified extensions of the standard cosmological models often introduce complex parameter degeneracies that severely impact sampling convergence of the parameter space while analyzing the model observationally. In this work, we present an accelerated Bayesian inference technique using a Heteroscedastic Deep Ensemble with Monte Carlo Dropout incorporating distance-gated local residual corrections to emulate complex likelihood surfaces and avoid extrapolation beyond the trained region. We demonstrate this methodology on a unified dark energy cosmological model equipped with Finsler geometry. The model is studied using the recent observational datasets, including Cosmic Chronometers (CC), Pantheon$+$SH$0$ES, and DESI DR$2$ BAO measurements. While the conventional sampling procedure struggles with slow mixing of parameter chains ($\tau_{max}=1578.3$), the neural network, specially trained densely in high likelihood regions, yields converged and highly resolved posterior distributions of the model parameters without significantly compromising the minimum chi-square value. We further discuss the results for physical inferences and also compare the present dark energy model with $\Lambda\text{CDM}$ statistically using AIC and BIC.
item.dc:creator: Shruti Seth, R. Chaubey
